lessonRef.unitTitle: Decision Analysis and Expected Value Capstone
lessonRef.title: Concept model C: weighing expected value against risk

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example is written more briefly. Fill in the reasoning it leaves out.

items.prompt: Costs $5, pays $40 with probability 1/10. Expected value?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $18 and pays out $399 with probability 1/57. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.
Option A has expected payoff $32 and Option B has expected payoff $16. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.
Option A; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.
Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between two people using a single fair coin flip.
choices: Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A game costs $10 to play. It pays $126 with probability 1/7 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $-10; the game is unfavourable to the player
$18; the game is favourable to the player
$8; the game is favourable to the player
$116; the game is favourable to the player

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $16 and pays out $48 with probability 1/24. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.
Option A has expected payoff $22 and Option B has expected payoff $45. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.
Option B; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.
Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between three people by rolling a standard die, assigning faces 1–3, 4–5, and 6.
choices: Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.
Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.

items.prompt: A game costs $26 to play. It pays $216 with probability 1/6 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $190; the game is favourable to the player
$-26; the game is unfavourable to the player
$10; the game is favourable to the player
$36; the game is favourable to the player
